To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. patients with schizophrenia generated fewer words than healthy controls on the semantic and the phonemic fluency tasks, 2. patients with schizophrenia showed a disproportionate impairment in the semantic fluency task relative to the phonemic fluence task, 3. patients with schizophrenia produced fewer cluster related words on both fluency tests, and 4. patients with schizophrenia made fewer switches on both fluency test.

(a) patients with schizophrenia generate fewer words, cluster related and switched words than healthy controls on the semantic and the phonemic fluency tasks; (b) the differences in cluster related words and switched words between patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls are explained by the total number of produced words; and (c) the disproportionate impairment in semantic flueny in schizophrenia is due to a differential deficit in clustering.
the disproportionate impairment in semantic verbal (word) fluency in schizophrenia is not explained by differential impairment in switching strategies.
